about: Starter content for the Discover mode (see docs/ROADMAP.md, work package 4). Written for a concept page on 2026-11-11 and checked by script: formulas agree with interval lists, numerals agree with offsets. Intervals and offsets are semitones above the key root. Adapt the shape to the app's own types when building.

sounds.name: Lydian dominant
sounds.vibe: Bright and sly. Major on top with a blues wink underneath.
sounds.ear: The ♯4 and the ♭7 in the same phrase. Neither one wants to resolve.
sounds.over: A 7 or 9 chord that is not the V of the key: a IV7 or a ♭VII7. Fourth mode of melodic minor.

sounds.name: Mixolydian ♭6
sounds.vibe: Heroic up top, wistful underneath. The film-score major.
sounds.ear: A major 3rd and a ♭6 in one breath: sunshine with a shadow across it.
sounds.over: A plain major triad, or a I chord that keeps falling to iv. Fifth mode of melodic minor.

sounds.name: Phrygian dominant
sounds.ear: The three-fret gap between ♭2 and 3, and the ♭2 falling home to the root.
sounds.over: A major chord rocking to the major chord a fret above it (I to ♭II). It is harmonic minor started from its 5th.

sounds.name: Double harmonic
sounds.ear: Two wide gaps (♭2 to 3, ♭6 to 7), each sitting next to a half step.
sounds.over: A major triad drone. Tremolo-pick it on one string.

sounds.name: Hungarian minor
sounds.vibe: Gothic and theatrical. Minor with two raised eyebrows.
sounds.ear: The ♯4 leaning up into the 5, and the 7 leaning up into the root.
sounds.over: A minor triad drone. Harmonic minor with the 4th pushed up a fret.

sounds.name: Hirajoshi
sounds.vibe: Koto tuning. Stark, spacious, a little cold.
sounds.ear: Two tight half steps (2 to ♭3, 5 to ♭6) with wide silence between them.
sounds.over: Root and fifth only. Play fewer notes than feels comfortable.

sounds.name: In-sen
sounds.vibe: Suspended and mysterious. No 3rd, so neither major nor minor.
sounds.ear: The ♭2 pressing against the root while the 4 and 5 stay wide open.
sounds.over: An open-fifth drone, or a sus4 chord.

sounds.name: Minor 6 pentatonic
sounds.vibe: Your blues box, one note smarter.
sounds.ear: The 6 where your hand expects the ♭7.
sounds.over: Minor 6 and minor 7 chords. In a blues, play it from the key note over the IV chord: the 6 is that chord’s 3rd.

sounds.name: Dominant pentatonic
sounds.vibe: Sweet and salty. Country bends with a jazz accent.
sounds.ear: Major pentatonic with the 6 traded for a ♭7.
sounds.over: Any dominant 7 or 9 chord. Bend the 2 up to the 3.

sounds.name: Whole tone
sounds.ear: No half steps anywhere, so nothing pulls toward home.
sounds.over: Augmented and 7♯5 chords. Every shape repeats two frets up: slide one idea up the neck.
sounds.heard: Stevie Wonder, “You Are the Sunshine of My Life” (intro)

sounds.name: Half–whole diminished
sounds.vibe: Coiled and angular. Tension with a pattern to it.
sounds.ear: Half step, whole step, forever. Eight notes, no resting place.
sounds.over: A dominant 7 that is about to resolve (13♭9). Every shape repeats three frets up.

sounds.name: Augmented scale
sounds.ear: Three major triads a major third apart, hiding in six notes.
sounds.over: A maj7 or maj7♯5 chord. Every shape repeats four frets up.

moves.name: I – III – IV – iv
moves.vibe: Yearning. A door opens, then the light changes.
moves.why: III is major where the key expects minor, and the last chord is IV turned minor, borrowed from the parallel key.
moves.over: Trace one inner line on a single string: 5, ♯5, 6, ♭6, back to 5. It is the melody hiding inside the chords.

moves.name: ♭VI – ♭VII – I
moves.why: Two major chords borrowed from the parallel minor climb by whole steps into a major home.
moves.over: Minor pentatonic over the first two chords, then land hard on the major 3rd when I arrives.

moves.name: i – ♭VII – ♭VI – V
moves.why: The bass walks down four steps to a major V, which snaps you back to the top.
moves.over: Natural minor all the way down. On the V chord raise the ♭7 to 7: that one note is harmonic minor.

moves.name: i7 – IV7
moves.vibe: A smoky groove that never needs to resolve.
moves.why: The IV chord is major, so the key’s 6th is natural. That single note is the whole Dorian sound.
moves.over: Minor pentatonic plus the natural 6, which is also the 3rd of the IV chord. Aim for it in bar two.

moves.name: Imaj7 – II/I
moves.why: A major triad one whole step up, over the same bass note, puts the ♯4 on top.
moves.over: Lydian. Hang on the ♯4 and never let it fall to the 4.
moves.heard: Joe Satriani, “Flying in a Blue Dream”

moves.name: Iadd9 – vi(add9) – IVadd9 – Vadd9
moves.why: Every chord wears a 9th, so the changes blur into one shimmering texture.
moves.over: Do not solo: arpeggiate. Stack two fifths (root, 5th, 9th) at frets +0, +2, +4 on three neighbouring low strings.

moves.name: i – ♭vi
moves.why: Two minor triads a major third apart share exactly one note. Everything else slides a half step.
moves.over: No single scale covers both. Hold the shared note (the ♭3 of the key) and arpeggiate around it.

moves.name: Imaj7 – ♭VImaj7 – IIImaj7
moves.vibe: Kaleidoscope. Three keys split the octave.
moves.why: The roots fall by major thirds until they land back home.
moves.over: Take one small idea and move it down four frets with each chord.
moves.heard: John Coltrane, “Giant Steps” (its three key centres)

moves.name: IVmaj7 – III7 – vi7 – v7 I7
moves.why: III7 is the V of vi. The last bar is a ii–V that drops you straight back onto IV.
moves.over: Major scale. Raise the 5 to ♯5 over III7, and lower the 7 to ♭7 over the last bar.
moves.heard: Grover Washington Jr. and Bill Withers, “Just the Two of Us”

moves.name: Imaj7 – iv7 – ♭VII7 – Imaj7
moves.vibe: The side entrance home. Warm, soulful.
moves.why: iv7 – ♭VII7 is a ii–V borrowed from the key a minor third up. It resolves up a whole step instead of down a fifth.
moves.over: Minor pentatonic through the middle two bars, then land on the major 3rd.

moves.name: ii7 – ♭II7 – Imaj7
moves.vibe: A chromatic glide into home. Bossa after dark.
moves.why: ♭II7 shares its 3rd and 7th with V7: same tension, but the bass slides down by half steps.
moves.over: Follow the bass: 2, ♭2, 1. Over ♭II7 try Lydian dominant from its root.

moves.name: i – i(maj7) – i7 – i6
moves.why: The chord never moves. One voice walks down: root, 7, ♭7, 6.
moves.over: Find that falling line on one string and let it be the melody.

lenses.name: Brightness dial
lenses.blurb: Seven modes, brightest to darkest. Each step flattens exactly one note.
lenses.prompt: Hold the drone. Step down one notch at a time and play only the note that just changed against the root.

variants.label: Ionian
variants.note: ♯4 drops to 4. The plain major scale.

variants.label: Mixolydian
variants.note: 7 drops to ♭7. Major with a blues edge.

variants.label: Dorian
variants.note: 3 drops to ♭3. Minor now, but the 6 keeps it warm.

variants.label: Locrian
variants.note: 5 drops to ♭5. Even home is unstable.

lenses.name: One string
lenses.blurb: Mick Goodrick’s first lesson: improvise along a single string.
lenses.prompt: Pick a string and play melodies along it with one finger. Box licks stop working, and you start hearing distances.

lenses.name: Three notes
lenses.blurb: A hand of three notes. Rhythm and phrasing do the rest.
lenses.prompt: Deal three notes. Play only those, anywhere on the neck, for one minute. Change the rhythm, the octave and the attack before you ask for more notes.

lenses.name: Pentatonic swap
lenses.blurb: The box you already know, started from a different note of the chord.
lenses.prompt: Over a maj7 chord, play a minor pentatonic box from each of these notes. Same fingering, new colours.

variants.label: From the 6th
variants.note: The usual one, the relative minor box: R 2 3 5 6. Safe and sweet.

variants.label: From the 3rd
variants.note: No root at all: 2 3 5 6 7. It sounds like the top half of the chord.

variants.label: From the 7th
variants.note: Adds the ♯4: 2 3 ♯4 6 7. Instant Lydian from a blues box.

lenses.name: Triad pairs
lenses.blurb: Two neighbouring major triads, alternated. Structured, modern, and hard to play a cliché with.
lenses.prompt: Play one triad going up and the other coming down, and keep leapfrogging up the neck.

variants.label: I + II
variants.note: Over a maj7 chord: the Lydian pair.

variants.label: ♭VII + I
variants.note: Over a dominant 7 chord: the Mixolydian pair.

variants.label: ♭III + IV
variants.note: Over a minor 7 chord: the Dorian pair.

lenses.name: Side-slip
lenses.blurb: Go outside on purpose, then come home.
lenses.prompt: Play a phrase in the box. Shift the same fingering up one fret for two beats (the dashed rings), then drop back and land on a chord tone.

sparks: Leave two full beats of silence after every phrase.
Play only on the G and B strings.
Start every phrase on the “and” of 2.
Play a phrase. Now play it again a third higher.
End every phrase on the 3rd of the chord.
Sing the next phrase first, then find it.
Slide into every note from one fret below.
Play as quietly as you can. Then one note loud.
No note shorter than a half note.
Take the rhythm of your own name. Put any notes on it.
Stay inside four frets. Do not leave.
Skip a string on every jump.
Repeat one bar four times. Change exactly one note each time.
Start where you would normally end.
Bend up to every chord tone instead of fretting it.
Two bars climbing, two bars falling.
Play the same three notes in five different places.
